business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of PC and Console Video Games via Digital Stores

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between Spain and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income, signed 1990, as amended by Protocol of 2013
EU-Peru Trade Agreement (in force since 1 March 2013)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Ley 6/2023 and Real Decreto-ley 7/2021; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010 on money laundering and UBO registers; Directive (EU) 2015/849, as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD4/AMLD5); Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital regarding corporate formation and registered office.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each natural-person shareholder and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or competent civil registry in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if country of origin is not a Hague Convention party, Consular Legalization by the Spanish Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing and corporate extract of each corporate shareholder, identifying directors and beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies or corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if non-Hague jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (Poder) for the incorporator or founding attorney-in-fact
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the grantor's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; internal signature verification by the executing Spanish notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Spanish translation of all apostilled corporate and identity documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator appointed by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs or by the relevant linguistic institute
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled underlying document remains valid; sworn translation itself is attached without a second apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of deposit of share capital (Certificado de depósito del capital social)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish-licensed credit institution holding the SL initial capital deposit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Submitted directly to the public notary at execution of the deed; no apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners are screened against the consolidated EU financial sanctions list (European External Action Service), UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, Her Majesty's Treasury UK sanctions list, SEPBLAC registry of suspicious operators, and domestic police and tax enforcement lists. PEP identification is mandatory under Article 14 of Ley 10/2010; enhanced due diligence is applied to politically exposed persons, high-risk geographic areas, and any Steam or PlayStation payout channel revealing unusual transaction patterns. In light of ECJ judgment C-37/20 and Ley 6/2023, UBO data is not generally public but is disclosed to SEPBLAC, the Central Commercial Registry, notaries, and AML-obliged entities on a legitimate-interest basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) online name clearance service, accessible through the Colegio de Registradores de España portal at www.registradores.org and the legacy RMC web portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed corporate names must be submitted in Spanish. Foreign words and trademarks may be accepted when written in Latin script, readily pronounceable in Spanish, and not misleading; if a non-Latin script is used, a transliteration into Latin characters is mandatory. The corporate name must contain the legal form phrase 'Sociedad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'SL' at the beginning or end. Names identical to or confusingly similar to an existing registered name are rejected; descriptive names in Spanish are allowed where they accurately describe the business activity, which for this scope is publishing of PC and console video games via digital stores (CNAE 5820).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Mercantil Central rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written administrative grievance within one month from notification under Law 39/2015 (LPACAP). The registry re-examines the grounds; if sustained, the applicant may appeal to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within the statutory appeal period. A replacement name may be submitted concurrently. Because the negative name certificate is valid for 90 days, a fresh certificate must be obtained if the reservation expires before notarial execution; an extension may be requested only if made before the expiry date and before incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A PO box, mail-forwarding center, or purely virtual address without physical presence is not acceptable as the statutory registered domicile under Article 9 of Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, which requires the registered office to be in Spain and to correspond to the actual place of management or principal activity. A physical managed office, co-working space, or serviced office may qualify if it is a real street address, is accessible, appears in the deed of incorporation, and allows receipt of notices and visits from public authorities. Full virtual office registration is not permitted for a Spanish SL.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: less than 3% estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection during the first full accounting year for a low-risk online video game publishing company. However, inspection risk is materially increased if the registered office does not pass a substance review, or during initial tax/VAT registration where Agencia Tributaria (AEAT) may verify physical premises. SEPBLAC, Social Security authorities, and local licensing bodies also retain inspection rights.

Preparation and execution of the public deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial fee schedule (arancel notarial) based on share capital and deed complexity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registry filing fee for the SL incorporation (inscripción de la sociedad)
Apostille or consular legalization of foreign shareholder, UBO, and corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in country of origin / Spanish Consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government fee plus courier; prevailing per-document market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn Spanish translation of apostilled foreign corporate and identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator appointed by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate per translated page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration (titularidad real) and AML/CFT compliance file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market legal fee for Stage 1 due diligence file

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Oficina de Extranjería / Dirección General de la Policía

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank certificate of initial capital deposit
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank service fee for capital deposit certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence, virtual office substance assessment, and pre-corporate tax/AML gap analysis
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed fee or hourly attorney benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 4, 19-23, 33-35, 58-62, 210-245, and 285-289; Law 14/2013 and Law 18/2022 on streamlined electronic formation procedures also apply where used.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the province in which the registered office is located, coordinated by the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), followed by registration with the competent Provincial Commercial Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1.00. Until equity reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000, and shareholders may bear subsidiary liability for the difference between EUR 3,000 and the company's assets on liquidation. There is no general mandatory escrow account. A bank deposit certificate may evidence cash contributions, although founders may generally assume joint liability for the reality of contributions where legally permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The directors resolve that the Company accept and record the subscription and payment of its entire share capital by the incorporators in accordance with the incorporation deed and Articles of Association; adopt as its registered office the address stated in the deed; approve the corporate purpose of digital publishing and distribution of PC and console video games; appoint [Name] as sole director for the statutory term; authorize the director to obtain the NIF, complete Commercial Registry filings, open bank and payment accounts, and execute all documents required for lawful commencement of business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), through its online name-certificate service or authorized filing representative.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names and request a negative name certificate. Verify that the proposed name includes the legal designation Sociedad Limitada or S.L. The certificate should be issued in the name of an incorporator and remain valid for the statutory period. Provide an apostilled and sworn-translated power of attorney where a representative acts for a non-resident incorporator.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, select an alternative name and resubmit. If the certificate contains an error, request correction before execution of the incorporation deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foreign Identification and Prepare Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria) and a Spanish notary public (notario).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain NIE numbers for foreign individual directors or shareholders and NIF numbers for foreign corporate shareholders where required. Prepare the Articles of Association, corporate purpose, capital and share allocation, registered office, management structure, director acceptance, beneficial ownership information, and evidence of capital contributions. Foreign public documents must normally be apostilled or legalized and accompanied by an official Spanish translation.
required_dossiers: Corporate certificates of incorporation and authority for corporate shareholders
Evidence of capital contribution or statutory founder declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct identification, translation, legalization, beneficial ownership, or corporate-authority defects before the notarial appointment. Obtain replacement certificates if validity periods have expired.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public with territorial competence for the incorporation transaction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators or duly authorized attorneys must sign the public deed. The notary verifies identity, capacity, name reservation, capital subscription, Articles of Association, management appointment, beneficial ownership, and legality of the corporate purpose. Ensure that the deed expressly identifies the registered office, share capital, individual share numbers, management system, and director acceptance.
required_dossiers: Capital contribution evidence or permitted founder declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve notarial observations by supplying missing evidence, correcting the Articles, or issuing a supplemental deed. Do not submit an incomplete or unsigned deed for registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company with the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the registered-office province, usually through the notary's electronic filing platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed public deed, pay the applicable tariff-based registry charges, and request registration. The registry examines legal compliance and records the company, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, and directors. Obtain the registration notice and updated registry information after completion. The company acquires full legal personality upon registration.
required_dossiers: Registry filing form or electronic submission
Proof of payment of registry charges
Corrective or supplemental deed, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a qualification notice is issued, cure the stated defect within the applicable period through corrected documents, a supplemental deed, or an appeal to the Directorate-General for Legal Security and Public Faith (Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Beneficial Ownership, and Operational Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency; Provincial Commercial Registry; and the relevant municipality or Autonomous Community authority for premises-related activities.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain or confirm the provisional and definitive NIF using Form 036, register the appropriate IAE economic activity heading, and file beneficial ownership information when required. Register for VAT and intra-Community VAT operations if applicable. For a physical office, studio, warehouse, or customer-facing premises, submit the applicable municipal activity notification, responsible declaration, opening communication, or prior operating license before commencing regulated premises use.
required_dossiers: Registered public deed and Commercial Registry details
Municipal responsible declaration or activity notification, if applicable
Fire and technical compliance documents, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to tax or municipal requests within the stated deadline, amend Form 036 or the activity filing, and submit missing technical certificates. Suspend the affected premises activity until required municipal or safety clearance is obtained.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sector-specific industrial licensing board is ordinarily required for digital publication and online distribution of video games. The relevant authority for any physical installation is the competent Autonomous Community industry authority and the municipality where the premises are located.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No national manufacturing or industrial operating permit for digital game publishing. A municipal activity communication, responsible declaration, opening communication, or prior activity license may be required for offices, studios, warehouses, or other premises, depending on the municipality and the physical activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico), together with the competent environmental body of the relevant Autonomous Community.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt or not applicable for ordinary digital publishing, software distribution, and office operations that do not constitute a project listed in Annexes I or II of Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment. A separate assessment may apply to construction, major installations, or listed industrial projects.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, industrial VOC emissions, or manufacturing waste are ordinarily generated by the stated activity. The company must manage office and electronic waste through authorized systems, comply with municipal wastewater rules, prevent unauthorized discharges, and obtain separate permits for any generator, storage, emission, or discharge installation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For ordinary office-based digital publishing, no national industrial clearance is generally required. Any premises must comply with applicable municipal fire-prevention rules, the Spanish Building Code, emergency access and evacuation requirements, electrical and structural safety standards, and Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention. Fire protection certificates, structural load assessments, accessibility reports, or workplace clearances may be required for studios, warehouses, server facilities, or premises undergoing works.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) with official portal at https://www.agenciatributaria.gob.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish SL entities obtain NIF upon registration with the Registro Mercantil Central. Foreign entities establishing Spanish branches or subsidiaries must apply to AEAT with incorporation deed, fiscal domicile proof, and other statutory documents to procure NIF and VAT identification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available under Spanish law. However, hybrid mismatch rules pursuant to ATAD apply to prevent treaty shopping and base erosion.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing via Facturae standard. SII system requires real-time or periodic transmission of invoice data to AEAT through secure API connections with digital stamping and clearance protocols.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: VAT zero-rating for exports of goods outside the EU upon proof of export. For digital services and software, zero-rating applies to supplies to non-EU customers where the service is not effectively used in Spain, subject to customer location verification and reverse charge for intra-EU B2B.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent claims of export zero-rating result in fines equivalent to 100% of the VAT amount evaded, plus interest and potential criminal liability under Spanish Penal Code for tax fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), ... plus European Central Bank (ECB) as eurozone monetary authority.  Also SEPBLAC ...
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a eurozone member; the euro is fully freely convertible under Articles 63-65 TFEU and the EU Capital Movements Directive (88/361/EEC). No current-account or capital-account restrictions; a universal balance-of-payments statistical declaration regime applies (Circular 4/2007, Banco de España) ...
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None; no mandatory sale or surrender of export receipts is imposed on Spanish resident companies. Receipts may be freely held in divisible foreign currency. Only statistical reporting thresholds apply (declaration to the Banco de España on Forms BE-9/BE-8 where transactions exceed €50,000 per individual operation, cumulative monthly thresholds, or annual thresholds; banks collect the declaration when the client codes the transaction)...

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Filing (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil of the company's registered province
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval by June 30 (within 6 months after fiscal year-end); deposit within 1 month after approval, i.e., by July 30 for calendar-year filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure (cierre registral) after two consecutive missed filings, blocking any corporate registry act; fines EUR 300–EUR 6,000; administrative dissolution procedure after 3 years of non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year companies: due by July 25 (25th day of the 7th month after fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty EUR 150–EUR 1,500 if no tax due; if tax is due, 150% surcharge on the unpaid amount plus late-payment interest and possible executive seizure of assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Declaration (Declaración de Identificación del Titular Real)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (attached to annual accounts filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted together with annual accounts, no later than July 30 for calendar-year filers; must be updated upon any change in beneficial ownership of 25% or more
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance constitutes an anti-money-laundering infringement under Law 10/2010; serious breaches may trigger fines up to EUR 60,000 and suspension of registry operations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Third-Party and Related-Party Operations Information Return (Form 347 / Form 232)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Form 347: for transactions with third parties exceeding EUR 3,005.06 in the preceding year, due March 1; Form 232 (related-party transactions exceeding EUR 250,000): due within 1 month after filing Form 200
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Form 347 penalties: EUR 100 per unsupplied item with a minimum EUR 1,500; if the omission affects taxable amounts, a 75% penalty on the undervalued amount. Form 232 non-compliance can carry fines up to EUR 15,000

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit required if a company exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds in two consecutive fiscal years: total assets above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover above EUR 8,000,000; average workforce above 50 employees. An audit may also be mandated by shareholders representing at least 5% shareholding or by the Commercial Registry in specific circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad – Real Decreto 1514/2007, as amended by Real Decreto 1159/2010); the abbreviated PYMES framework is available for eligible smaller entities; IFRS as adopted by the EU applies to consolidated groups and entities listed in EU regulated markets.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The annual UBO confirmation must be filed with the Registro Mercantil concurrently with the annual accounts. The declaration must identify every individual who ultimately owns or controls more than 25% of the SL, directly or indirectly. Any share transfer must be recorded in the Libro Registro de Socios, and if such transfer alters the 25% ownership/control threshold, an updated UBO declaration must be submitted with the next annual filing or immediately if a new reportable owner appears.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Registro de Consejeros) – appointments and resignations filed at the Mercantile Registry
Inventory and Annual Accounts Book (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 1,500–4,200 USD (approx. EUR 150–350 per month for a registered office, corporate secretarial and AML compliance service)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,000–8,000 USD (approx. EUR 2,800–7,400 for an SME statutory audit conducted by a registered Spanish auditor)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general Corporate Income Tax rate. Qualifying newly created companies generally apply 15% to the first positive taxable base and the following tax period, subject to statutory conditions. Qualifying micro-enterprises may benefit from reduced rates under applicable annual legislation.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Spain provides deductions and credits for qualifying research and development, technological innovation, audiovisual and video-game production, foreign tax paid, and certain investments. Tax losses may be offset subject to annual limitations generally based on turnover: 70% of the taxable base for taxpayers with turnover below EUR 20 million, 50% for turnover from EUR 20 million to below EUR 60 million, and 25% for turnover of EUR 60 million or more, in each case subject to a EUR 1 million minimum offset. Qualifying newly created companies and certain restructuring transactions may be subject to special rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited; Spain does not impose a general five-year expiry. Utilization remains subject to statutory annual percentage limitations, the EUR 1 million minimum threshold, anti-abuse rules, and the continuity and verification rules applicable to tax losses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Declaración del Impuesto sobre Sociedades e Impuesto sobre la Renta de no Residentes, régimen de tributación por el establecimiento permanente. Mandatory electronic filing through the Spanish Tax Agency Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria electronic office using an electronic certificate or qualifying electronic identification.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year company ending on 31 December, the ordinary deadline is generally 25 July of the following year, subject to calendar-day and electronic-filing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number, registered office, tax period start and end dates, legal form, activity classification, and filing type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or parent does not replace the Spanish SL's own identification. The Spanish SL files under its Spanish tax identification number. A permanent establishment of a non-resident uses its own Modelo 200 permanent-establishment filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before Corporate Income Tax from the statutory accounts prepared under Spanish accounting rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only the Spanish entity's accounting result. Do not consolidate foreign parent or group accounts unless a specific tax consolidation regime applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Positive and negative adjustments for non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, impairment, exempt income, transfer-pricing adjustments, hybrid mismatches, and other Spanish tax-law differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding taxes and foreign expenses require separate validation for deductibility, treaty relief, foreign-tax-credit treatment, and documentary evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after adjustments and offset of carried-forward tax losses, subject to annual limitations and anti-abuse provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SL may not use losses of a foreign shareholder or affiliate merely because it belongs to the same group. Related-party loss transfers require a statutory tax-consolidation or restructuring basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable statutory or preferential rate multiplied by the taxable base, including rate selection for newly created companies or other qualifying regimes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 15% new-company rate is not automatic and requires satisfaction of the statutory definition and exclusion conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable deductions for research and development, technological innovation, audiovisual or video-game production, foreign tax, employment or qualifying investments, where supported by statutory requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign group development costs cannot be claimed as Spanish credits without Spanish qualifying activity, eligible expenditure, and required certificates or supporting records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Payments on account and withholding credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior Modelo 202 payments, Spanish withholding tax, and other creditable payments attributable to the tax period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit only Spanish taxes supported by certificates or Agencia Tributaria records. Foreign withholding is generally dealt with under the foreign-tax-credit rules and applicable treaty limitation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net Corporate Income Tax payable or refundable after credits and payments on account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any refund claim must be supported by bank, accounting, and tax records and may trigger verification before payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of related-party transactions and applicable transfer-pricing documentation or reporting information where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose transactions with non-resident group companies, including platform, licensing, financing, management, development, and cost-sharing arrangements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Required financial, tax, related-party, loss, deduction, and group-regime schedules accompanying the electronic return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain Spanish statutory accounts, intercompany agreements, invoices, payout statements from Steam or console platforms, royalty records, and evidence of services received.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: A late return without tax payable generally attracts a fixed penalty of EUR 200, normally reduced by 50% for voluntary filing without prior notice where the statutory conditions are met. A late return producing a tax loss or other adverse effect may attract EUR 200 or EUR 400, depending on the case. Where tax is payable and the filing is late, the surcharge is generally 1% plus an additional 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus late-payment interest. Incorrect or incomplete returns may attract penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, with higher exposure for concealment, false invoices, or fraudulent conduct.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, pagos fraccionados del Impuesto sobre Sociedades, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency electronic office.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payment installments, where mandatory or voluntarily applicable
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally 1 to 20 April, October, and December. The filing and payment deadline generally extends to 15 April, October, or December where direct debit is used, subject to current electronic-office rules. Mandatory filing generally applies where the prior 12-month net turnover exceeds EUR 6 million; the applicable calculation method depends on statutory conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish tax identification number, legal name, tax period, and installment period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL files under its own tax number. A foreign parent is not substituted as taxpayer unless the applicable Spanish group tax regime legally designates a representative or group entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year liability method or current-period taxable-base method, as legally applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the method based on Spanish statutory thresholds and elections. Do not use foreign consolidated EBITDA, revenue, or tax figures as substitutes for Spanish tax data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relevant prior-year tax liability or current-period tax base and adjustments used to calculate the installment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude non-Spanish group results unless legally included under a Spanish consolidation regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable statutory percentage, resulting payment, and credits or prior payments where permitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile each installment with the accounting ledger, cash payments, and the subsequent Modelo 200.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount payable, payment reference, or zero filing where the form is required but no amount is due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A zero or loss position does not automatically remove a filing obligation where Modelo 202 is mandatory.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment may generate statutory surcharges, late-payment interest, and enforcement costs. Incorrect or omitted installments may produce tax penalties generally based on the underpaid amount. The annual Modelo 200 remains the final settlement and does not eliminate liability for deficient interim payments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding on dividends paid by a Spanish company to a non-resident, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable tax treaties. The EU Parent-Subsidiary exemption may eliminate withholding where the statutory conditions are satisfied, commonly including qualifying EU parent status, a minimum 10% participation held for at least one year or an undertaking to hold it, subject-to-tax requirements, and anti-abuse conditions. Spanish domestic participation-exemption rules may also apply to Spanish-resident corporate recipients.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority and verify beneficial ownership, treaty entitlement, limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse provisions, minimum holding conditions, and any applicable EU exemption. Apply the treaty or exemption at source only where the payer has adequate evidence and the Spanish procedural requirements are met; otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and allow the recipient to seek a refund using the applicable Spanish Tax Agency procedure. Maintain ownership charts, certificates, declarations, agreements, payment records, and evidence that the recipient is not an intermediary or conduit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Spanish non-resident income tax rate is generally 24% on gross royalties and interest paid to non-residents, reduced to 19% for residents of another EU Member State or an EEA jurisdiction with effective exchange-of-information arrangements, subject to applicable statutory exclusions. Interest and royalty payments between qualifying associated companies in different EU Member States may be exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive as implemented in Spain, subject to qualifying ownership, minimum holding, subject-to-tax, beneficial-owner, and anti-abuse conditions. Tax treaties commonly reduce rates and may provide exclusive residence-state taxation for certain interest; the treaty applicable to the recipient must be checked individually.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 45 million consolidated group turnover is the principal threshold for mandatory Master File preparation under the general Spanish documentation framework. A Local File is generally required for material related-party transactions, subject to statutory exemptions and simplified documentation for qualifying smaller entities. Transactions of the same type with the same related party generally benefit from a documentation exemption where their aggregate arm's-length value does not exceed EUR 250,000 in the tax period, subject to exclusions and special rules, including transactions involving tax havens or specified high-risk categories. Spain's specific-country reporting and documentation thresholds must be separately tested.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no standalone UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Nevertheless, Spanish anti-abuse, beneficial-ownership, transfer-pricing, controlled-foreign-company, hybrid-mismatch, general anti-avoidance, and business-purpose rules require genuine functions, assets, risks, decision-making, and commercial substance. A Spanish SL publishing games should evidence Spanish personnel or contractors, management control, platform contracts, IP rights, marketing and localization functions, financial capacity, and operational decision-making. Contractual allocation of profit without corresponding functions, assets, and risks may be recharacterized or adjusted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent Corporate Income Tax filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales or platform payouts, issuing or using false invoices, fabricating deductible costs, deliberately understating royalties or related-party income, or claiming unsupported tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, with interest and collection costs. Where the tax quota defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 in a tax period, the conduct may constitute a criminal tax offense punishable generally by imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded, together with loss of public subsidies and tax benefits for a period of three to six years. Aggravated cases may carry imprisonment of two to six years and a fine of two to six times the amount defrauded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil liability for tax debts in cases of culpable or negligent failure to discharge statutory duties, and criminal liability where they personally participate or knowingly facilitate the offense. Courts may order restitution, fines, disqualification, and imprisonment. Travel restrictions are exceptional judicial measures and are not automatic consequences of a tax assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unreported digital-platform income and VAT misclassification
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Excluding Steam or console-store settlements from Spanish books, failing to reconcile gross consumer receipts with platform net payouts, applying incorrect place-of-supply rules, or omitting intra-EU digital-service reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of unpaid Corporate Income Tax and VAT, late-payment interest, surcharges, and administrative penalties generally calculated by reference to the unpaid or incorrectly documented tax. Serious or repeated conduct may trigger higher penalties and criminal exposure where the relevant criminal thresholds are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face subsidiary liability for unpaid tax where statutory derivation conditions are satisfied, particularly after failure to comply with a tax assessment or deliberate obstruction. Criminal liability requires personal participation or legally relevant cooperation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially shifting Spanish publishing profits to a foreign affiliate through excessive royalties, management fees, financing costs, platform commissions, or unsupported cost-sharing arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish Tax Agency may make an arm's-length adjustment, assess additional tax and interest, impose documentation or inaccurate-return penalties, and apply withholding tax to recharacterized payments. Failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation may attract specific fixed penalties and percentage-based penalties linked to the adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur administrative or civil liability where they approved knowingly unsupported arrangements or failed to maintain required records. Criminal liability requires intentional fraudulent conduct and satisfaction of the criminal tax thresholds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive treaty shopping and beneficial-ownership failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing dividends, interest, or royalties through a conduit entity lacking commercial substance, withholding tax residence, beneficial ownership, or genuine decision-making capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Treaty or domestic exemption denial, withholding at the Spanish domestic rate, assessment of unpaid withholding tax and interest, and administrative penalties. Anti-abuse provisions may recharacterize the arrangement and deny EU Parent-Subsidiary or Interest and Royalties Directive relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Spanish payer and responsible officers may be liable for failure to withhold or pay over tax. Personal criminal exposure requires knowing and material participation in fraud; imprisonment and judicial travel restrictions are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False invoicing, accounting manipulation, or destruction of records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating fictitious invoices, backdating intercompany agreements, recording non-existent development services, deleting platform statements, or maintaining parallel accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax penalties, denial of deductions, tax assessments, and possible criminal offenses relating to tax fraud, accounting falsification, or document falsification. Criminal penalties may include imprisonment, fines, and disqualification depending on the offense and facts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, finance officers, and external participants may be personally prosecuted where they ordered, authorized, or knowingly used false records. Civil restitution, fines, professional disqualification, and imprisonment may apply following judicial conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained investor funds, concealing the ultimate beneficial owner, using nominee shareholders, transferring proceeds through high-risk jurisdictions, or failing to maintain customer, supplier, and beneficial-owner records where the entity falls within an applicable regulated-obligor category.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious breaches may generate fines for legal entities and responsible individuals, public or private reprimands, authorization restrictions, removal or disqualification of management, and other statutory measures. Criminal money-laundering or sanctions-related conduct may carry imprisonment and substantial fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face personal administrative sanctions and criminal liability for knowing participation, grossly negligent facilitation, concealment, or obstruction. Asset freezing, confiscation, judicial travel restrictions, and imprisonment require the applicable administrative or judicial process.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared permanent establishment or hidden Spanish management
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the publishing business from Spain while contractually or formally attributing sales, IP exploitation, or strategic management to a foreign affiliate without reporting a Spanish taxable presence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish Tax Agency may assess Corporate Income Tax, VAT, withholding tax, interest, and penalties for the relevant periods and may recharacterize the foreign arrangement as a Spanish permanent establishment or Spanish-resident management structure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur subsidiary tax liability and, where intentional concealment is proven, criminal tax exposure. Corporate separateness is not disregarded merely because a group operates cross-border; veil piercing requires exceptional facts such as fraud, abuse of legal personality, or unlawful asset diversion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper dividend distribution and insolvency conduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits without approved accounts or distributable reserves, returning capital while creditors are prejudiced, or paying dividends while the company is insolvent or unable to meet tax liabilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Invalid or recoverable distributions, shareholder repayment obligations, creditor claims, director liability under company and insolvency law, and potential criminal exposure for asset concealment or creditor prejudice.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to restore assets, compensate creditors, cover an insolvency deficit in qualifying cases, and face disqualification. Imprisonment or travel restrictions require separate judicial findings and are not automatic.
